children: shares rose 15% after the company posted higher revenue and cash generation for its fiscal first quarter, helped by growth across its operations.
Revenue reached $343.9 million, up 13.2% from a year earlier, while organic sales growth was 7%. Adjusted EBITDA also advanced 10%, indicating higher earnings from the company's operations.
Cash generation improved during the quarter. Operating cash flow increased by $25.7 million to $66.7 million, while free cash flow almost doubled to $54 million.

Worthington also pointed to demand for its engineered ASME tanks, which are used in liquid cooling applications at data centers. Chief Executive Officer Joe Hayek said the company is seeing increased interest tied to that market.

Capital returns were another part of the quarter. The company bought back 335,000 shares for $18.2 million and approved a quarterly dividend of $0.20 per share. The combination of stronger financial results, rising cash flow and continued shareholder returns helped drive the stock's gain.

title: Worthington Enterprises Shares Jump 15% on Strong Earnings and Cash Flow Boost
